info.cls_ename: SJSU-FCU 2+2 Bachelor's Program in Electrical Engineering

description.describe_ch: This course is an introduction to physics. The main emphasis will be on the branch of physics known as mechanics. This is the study of motion and the causes of motion through the applications of fundamental principles of physics. We begin with kinematics, the quantitative description of the motion of particles. We then build on kinematics to learn how and why motion occurs, through the application of Newton's laws of dynamics. Many examples will be considered as we explore the properties of specific forces and the details of the motion they bring about. The next step will be to describe physical processes in terms of energy and momentum, quantities that are always "conserved." Conservation laws allow us to solve problems in mechanics that would be very difficult by other techniques and provide a powerful approach to the analysis of physical systems in general. We then will extend our understanding of motion to the kinematics and dynamics of rotation. Finally, we will briefly study some of the physical properties of solids and fluids.

targets.describe_ch: Capability to understand most of natural phenomena in physics science with a few fundamental principles and laws of physics associated with dynamics and thermal physics
targets.describe_en: Capability to understand most of natural phenomena in physics science with a few fundamental principles and laws of physics associated with dynamics and thermal physics

targets.describe_ch: Ability to systematically approach problems behaving from microscopically to macroscopically, such as the evolution from classical dynamics to quantized atomic systems, or the leading from mechanics to basic thermodynamics
targets.describe_en: Ability to systematically approach problems behaving from microscopically to macroscopically, such as the evolution from classical dynamics to quantized atomic systems, or the leading from mechanics to basic thermodynamics

targets.describe_ch: Capability to describe topics of natural phenomena graphically and numerically by way of computer simulations using Easy Java Simulation and Matlab, without intensive training in Mathematics and Programming
targets.describe_en: Capability to describe topics of natural phenomena graphically and numerically by way of computer simulations using Easy Java Simulation and Matlab, without intensive training in Mathematics and Programming

targets.describe_ch: Experience to perform simple physical and virtual experiments, using computers and a variety of physics apparatus, including the gathering, interpretation and analysis of experimental data.
targets.describe_en: Experience to perform simple physical and virtual experiments, using computers and a variety of physics apparatus, including the gathering, interpretation and analysis of experimental data.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
1. 所有課程活動都將在同學、教師或助教間的友好參與和互動氛圍中進行，且彼此間尊重、欣賞、包容每個人的經歷、背景和觀點。 
2. 為確保有效學習環境，冀望每個人都能做到：言行禮貌、準時出席課堂；如有請假需求，請依照學校規定在請假系統提出申請。
3. 上課時段內勿進行與本課程無關事情，例如 閒聊、睡覺、進食(飲料不在此限)、划手機/打電動/上網....等。
4. 除非課程需要(如老師要求、學生作筆記...等)，學生會被要求將手機(或筆電、平板、耳機...等物件)放置到非觸手可及的位置(例如，書包袋子內、桌椅下方...等)。
5. 想與老師諮詢課業學生，建議提早一兩天與老師約定(當面或LINE訊息皆可)確認諮詢時間、地點。
    除非該位學生刻意表達希望是"一對一"諮詢，否則老師將公告此諮詢活動，並歡迎其他有興趣同學一併加入，以提升教與學的效率。
6. 課堂訊息(作業、考試、講義、.....等) 將以 (1) 課堂老師口頭或板書方式 或 (2) LINE群組 或 (3) iLearn公告 方式告知大家。
    如有彼此衝突，則以 (3)為最優先依據，(2)次之。
7. 學生亦可使用電子郵件(yinglee@o365.fcu.edu.tw)或LINE與老師連繫；但郵件要署名，老師不回覆“匿名”信件。
gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en: All course activities will be carried out in an atmosphere of friendly participation and interaction among students, respecting and appreciating each student's personal experience, background and perspectives, such as various school systems at home and abroad, diverse enrollment and learning cultures, gender, etc. You are expected to apply the highest academic standards throughout this course and to treat fellow students with dignity and respect.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem_en:
Students are welcome to contact the instructors through either the face-to-face comunications or the e-mail (yinglee@o365.fcu.edu.tw)

The instructor will approve students' requesting for class leave as long as the supporting document (in either photo or image format) is attached and fullfills one of the following situations：
1. It is not needed according to the related university regulations.
2. It is provided by the clinics or hospitals and it shows the student's name as well as the date of visiting.
3. It is provided by the departments of university or government for manatory events (such as the military service medical examination), and it shows the student's name

4. It is a memo with a brief description of the event and it MUST be signed by one of the following persons: 
    students' parents or guardians, the full-time prodessor of the department that the student belongs to. 

* A personal photo, a photo of the medicine bag or clinic buildings, a note without signatures from the person aforementioned...etc will not be accpeted as the supporting document.
